rehearsal.reason: the acceptance record judges this class; restart rehearsals are graded under deploy-restart

actual-volume-loss.meaning: actual volume loss alone in its zone provisions a replacement at the next generation and starts that shard cold; it is the only cold outcome of this record and never stands for host loss; the acceptance record judges it

staging.reason: actual volume loss has no live injection against the real provider

rehearsal.reason: the acceptance record judges this class; the correlated-loss hold release is graded under correlated-volume-loss

review.reason: the acceptance record judges this class and no reviewer item reads it

host-loss-multi-shard.meaning: a host that owns several shards and stands by for others is lost, partitioned or gray as the detector's corroborated suspicion reads it: each of its shards is taken over on its own standby host, which preempts the predecessor, at the same generation and volume, with no volume created; each successor fences coverage and loads warm, and under the END provider premise each retained set is served or lies on injected damage; each shard has a standby again within the settle bound or reports a named blocker

isolated-live-owner.meaning: an owner isolated from its peers while alive, with delayed writes, never shares a tenure with its successor; #148 and #137 own this case

model.reason: the isolated live owner rests on the END provider contract or the independent copy

simulation.reason: the fleet-world isolated-live-owner scenario is graded under isolated-live-owner-fleet

hardware.reason: the single-shard real-path qualification owns the isolated live owner on hardware

store.reason: the isolated live owner rests on the END provider contract or the independent copy

staging.reason: an isolated live owner with delayed writes has no staging package; it stays with #148 and #137

rehearsal.reason: no procedure acts on an isolated live owner apart from the host-loss procedures

review.reason: the END provider decision is reviewed under #148

isolated-live-owner-fleet.meaning: in the fleet world, an owner isolated from its peers while alive is preempted by its named standby, which takes the shard over at the same generation and volume with no volume created, fences coverage and loads warm; the isolated owner acknowledges no FILL or INVALIDATE after the preempt and never shares a tenure with its successor; the delayed-write qualification stays with isolated-live-owner

model.reason: the provider premise behind an isolated live owner is the END provider contract, which #148 decides

hardware.reason: the single-shard real-path qualification of #137 owns the isolated live owner on hardware

store.reason: the provider premise behind an isolated live owner is the END provider contract, which #148 decides

staging.reason: the fleet scenario runs in simulation; host-loss staging is graded under host-loss-multi-shard

observed-deposition.meaning: an owner that observes its deposition stops emission and withdraws, and the volume is retained

staging.reason: no staging package deposes a live owner on purpose; the fleet world and the deposition record judge it

unknown-write.meaning: a takeover, transfer, shard-record or coverage write with an unknown outcome licenses nothing and is followed by no device command; the writer continues only through the same-host restart, which recovers a committed write; after an unknown transfer write the withdrawn owner rereads the record and exits if it names the target, which activates through its own restart, or restarts once if it still names the withdrawn owner

staging.reason: an unknown write cannot be produced on purpose in staging; GD-11 rehearses it as a tabletop

store-outage.meaning: with the store unavailable, ownership writes and publication wait, INVALIDATE stays unacknowledged and hits of a current tenure continue

az-loss-return.meaning: an AZ outage leaves its shards dark or origin-served until the AZ returns; then each restarts, fences coverage before any admission and loads warm, with no generation change and no volume created

volume-impairment-hold.meaning: an impaired volume is retained with no replacement receipt, no generation change and nothing provisioned, and impairment of other volumes in its zone latches no hold; the reconciler orders no takeover, a takeover the owner host's false health bit starts may commit and then holds at the successor's device step, and the shard changes hands at most once; a shard the impairment leaves unserved reports a named blocker, and enabling I/O on the volume is an operator exit

isolated-volume-loss.meaning: in the fleet world, actual volume loss alone in its zone, confirmed in consecutive complete observations, changes only the lost shard, which ends as actual-volume-loss states with exactly one replacement volume across reconciler crashes and retries, counted as distinct volumes the provider created; every other shard keeps its tenure and refuses no request

staging.reason: actual volume loss has no live injection against the real provider; the fleet world judges it

correlated-volume-loss.meaning: actual loss of a shard's active volume while another volume of its zone is impaired or lost latches a replacement hold: no create reaches the provider from the held receipt, the hold stays after the other impairment clears, and only an operator's release ends it

staging.reason: a correlated actual volume loss has no live injection against the real provider; the fleet world judges the hold

owner-standby-loss.meaning: the owner and the standby of one shard are lost together: the reconciler attaches a fresh host to the surviving volume, which takes over warm, a new standby follows, and every shard without an injected fault keeps its tenure and refuses no request

successor-death.meaning: a successor that dies after its takeover write is recovered by the fresh-host path before its preempt and by its own restart after it; the volume is retained

staging.reason: a successor death between its takeover write and its preempt has no live injection; the fleet world judges it

retirement-request.meaning: a host-raised retirement request parks the owner and retains the volume and records; nothing is provisioned, an operator alarm fires and only an operator exit serves the request

staging.reason: staging holds no injection for the host-local evidence that raises a retirement request; the runbook rehearsal of #291 grades the operator exit

partition-loss.meaning: loss of a placement partition starts each lost shard's standby takeover as host loss does while the survivors' count of unvetoed suspected peers stays below the detector's self-suspicion threshold; at or above the threshold the survivors suspect themselves for the dwell, start no takeover, report a repair demand and a named blocker and retain every volume

deploy-restart.meaning: a deploy restarts hosts in place by color and zone under the admission gate; each restart is a same-host restart that loads warm, and a failed restart leaves the standby able to take over or a named blocker with the volume retained

planned-handoff.meaning: a planned handoff moves a shard to its named standby on the same volume with a warm load; a refused or unknown outcome ends in one same-host restart and the transfer write names no replacement standby

rollback-refusal.meaning: a release or rollback whose stored formats are incompatible is refused before any restart; a version change that would need a cold fleet is a refusal

control-plane-outage.meaning: a control-plane outage, a denied call included, is never read as volume or host loss: the reconciler defers and provisions nothing, and a standby takeover proceeds without it

reconciler-stop.meaning: with the zone reconciler stopped, each named standby still takes its shard over on the surviving volume and no volume is created; a predecessor that observes its deposition withdraws, no acknowledged invalidation is lost, and standby repair resumes when the reconciler returns

census-full.meaning: with the census at its cap, no shard gains a standby past the cap and no entry is evicted; each shard whose owner lives keeps serving and is reported in a named state apart from an enrollment in progress; a listed shard that loses its owner recovers through its named standby or a fresh host admitted in its own slot, and an unlisted shard that loses its owner retains its volume and generation, provisions nothing and reports the census refusal as a named blocker until a slot opens and a host loads it warm

attach-slots-exhausted.meaning: with a volume's attach slots exhausted, no attach passes the attachment bound until an ended attachment frees a slot; the shard keeps serving on its owner's attachment, and after owner loss a surviving host already attached to the volume can be designated and take over warm on that attachment; when recovery needs a new attach the bound refuses, the shard retains its volume and generation, provisions nothing and reports that refusal as a named blocker until a freed slot admits a host that loads it warm

power-loss.meaning: backend durability under host or volume power loss

model.reason: no case cuts volume power, and the acceptance record lists power loss unmeasured

simulation.reason: no case cuts volume power, and the acceptance record lists power loss unmeasured

hardware.reason: no hardware cell cuts volume power

store.reason: power loss changes no store record

staging.reason: no staging package cuts host or volume power

rehearsal.reason: power loss is handled by the host-loss procedures

review.reason: backend durability is owned by host-failure evidence on hardware

store-restore-reopen.meaning: the fleet reopens after an operator restores the store, which needs namespace and complete coverage evidence; TableId detection or a generation jump alone reopens nothing

model.reason: store qualification and restore reopening stay with the store owner
